questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I aimed at striking the right balance between the academic level and personal experiences/exploring new cultures. The most important was to:
1. A strong academic level
2. The amount of international students
3. The fact that Leuven is a major study city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The way exams are done/planned in Leuven makes it an 8/10 instead of 10/10.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Information was accessible and well communicated from the Faculty. Nothing to be worried about, as long as you followed the e-mails and deadlines set by the coordinators.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had to change my OLA, which they helped me with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It can be difficult, since housing market is short in Leuven. I recommend to search for relevant housing platforms via the university, since they collaborate with some off campus housing platforms.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You are still very close with the others living at campus, since the city is walkable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We were given around two weeks to try out different classes, before the final registration for courses. It helped me to get an overview of what courses felt "right", both with regard to the materials and especially the professor since they really have a big impact on how the course will be structured.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The incoming erasmus team via email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all the courses that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose as soon as possible, since it will be a bureaucratic process if you do not meet the deadline.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was satisfied, but very surprised that a 3 ECTS is treated like a 6 ECTS course or maybe even more, regarding the mandatory readings and so forth. Also, I found the course catalogue quite narrow with regard to my interest in law (financial/corporate law).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: KU Leuven Law only allow you to follow MA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A very different style of teaching. All classes are lectures with the professor presenting the material. Class participation varies from the professor while some "allow" it while others don't. Much more focus on powerpoints (they are a part of the mandatory readings) and the legislation itself. In most classes they do not have a course book or other materials related to the topic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Judicial Protection in the European Union (6 ECTS)
Restorative Justice (6 ECTS)
Political Crimes and Transitional Justice (6 ECTS)
International Arbitration (3 ECTS)
European Company Law (3 ECTS)
European Banking and Investment Services Law (4 ECTS)
Economic Analysis of Law (3 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
In general criminology courses. The credits match the workload and the exam is a written project + an oral part which is a good mix.

I was very excited about the banking law course and company law.

questions.answer: I had a gym membership at the uni-gym. It was also possible to opt for a culture card.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not attend myself, but I heard very well of the social running club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: To go around Belgium to see other cities. It is close by and easy to get there by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not a problem at all, not much different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The Belgian students are gone during the weekend, since they leave to see their parents. I did not really get a bond with any local students but more with the exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The beer production.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be aware of the academic preasure, since the exam schedule is very compressed. Also, exams are by hand and often with no tools/aid.
2. It is very easy to get a network in Leuven. Be open and you will have a very great time
3. Be proactive with housing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not anything that I have not already stated.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends and in general the social network that I got. Friends from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to the way of studying which is different from UCPH.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
